title: Earthquake
book_orientation: This is a recount. A girl tells about an earthquake that happened one night while she was at home with her mother.

lines: At about five o’clock last night,
I was in the kitchen
doing my homework
when I felt the table move.
Suddenly there was a big jolt.
Some of the water in my glass
splashed onto my book.
I grabbed the glass
as it slid towards me.
Mum rushed into the room.
She thought the jolt
might be an earthquake.
By now, Ginger, our old cat,
had jumped off my knee.
He disappeared behind the sofa.
Some of the things in the cupboards
began to rattle.
I was very scared now.
But Mum knew what to do.
She told me to climb under the table.
Then she crawled under the table, too.
She showed me
how to put my head down
between my knees.
The floor moved and I felt sick.
Mum made me hold tightly to a table leg.
She grabbed one of the others.
I closed my eyes and hoped
the shaking would stop soon.
Mum told me not to worry.

title: Harvest Mice
book_orientation: This is an information report about the smallest mice in the world—harvest mice.

lines: The harvest mouse
is the smallest mouse
in the world.
It is even smaller than the house mouse.
Many harvest mice live in fields of wheat.
Harvest mice can climb around
in tall grass and wheat
because they are so light.
They curl their long tails
around the wheat stalks,
and hold on with their back paws.
Harvest mice eat many things.
They like to eat berries,
small insects, new green leaves
and all kinds of seeds.
Harvest mice like wheat seeds.
They hold the seeds in their front paws.
Harvest mice are often in danger,
because foxes and weasels
hunt them on the ground.
Owls hunt them from the sky.
But when the wheat is tall and thick,
harvest mice have a good place to hide.
Owls and foxes
cannot see them, or hear them, in tall thick wheat.
Weasels cannot climb up wheat stalks.
If the mice build their nests
high up in the wheat, they are safe.
A mother mouse can make a nest quickly.

and shiny red apples.

have their own bakery.

title: Leo the Lion Cub
book_orientation: This story is about a lion cub whose mother died when he was only six weeks old.

lines: Leo belonged to a large family of lions,
called a pride.
When he was only six weeks old,
his mother died,
so his aunts took care of him.
Leo was the youngest
and smallest cub in the pride.
All of his cousins were bigger than he was.
They often knocked him over
when they played with him.
They liked pouncing on his tail,
and biting it.
Leo had to be brave.
He had to learn how to fight.
Soon it was time
for the pride to move on.
The lions needed to find
a new hunting ground.
They padded off through the dry grass,
one after the other.
But Leo could not keep up.
His little legs were too short.
When Leo whimpered,
one of his aunts stopped.
He tried to catch up with her,
but he could not walk fast enough.
So she moved on without him.
He was soon left behind.
He had never been alone before,
and he was afraid.

title: My New Aquarium
book_orientation: This text is a recount. A girl tells how her dad helped her set up a new aquarium.

lines: Last Friday,
Mrs Paul came over to our house.
She lived nearby
but was moving to a new home.
Mrs Paul was carrying
a small glass tank.
She knew I had always wanted
an aquarium and wondered
if I would like to have it.
Dad said he would help me set it up.
Later that morning,
Dad carried the tank outside
because he wanted to check
that it didn’t leak.
First he placed it on some paper.
Then he filled it with cold water.
After lunch, the paper was still dry.
We didn’t notice any leaks.
The tank was a bit dirty.
So I cleaned it with warm water.
Mum gave me a bag
of small brown stones.
I washed those, too.
Dad carried the empty tank inside.
He said it would be too heavy to move
when it was filled with water.
He put the tank on a small table
in the living room.
Mum brought in the stones
that I had washed earlier.

title: Akito’s Glasses
book_orientation: This text is a narrative. Akito is embarrassed about wearing glasses to school.

lines: “Hey, look at Akito! He’s wearing glasses!” Jack yelled.
“Yeah, doesn’t he look lovely!” grinned another boy.
Akito was really upset about having to wear his new
glasses to school. He knew some of the boys in his
class would tease him.
His best friend, Kris, sensed how he felt. “Don’t listen
to them, Akito,” he said quietly. “Remember, we’ve
got the cross-country race this afternoon and I’m sure
you’ll do well. If you win, you’ll go through to the
zone final.”
Later, as the boys lined up for the race, Kris and
Akito heard Jack say, “Watch out for Four Eyes. He
could trip over his feet!” Several boys nearby laughed.
But Kris and Akito took no notice.
At the starter’s signal, Kris and Akito ran side by side
in the middle of the group. Then, as they rounded
the bend by the school gym, they made their move.
Before long, they had left everyone else behind and
were leading the race.
“Let’s go!” Akito called to Kris. “I can see the finish
line in the distance.”
“You go!” gasped Kris. “I can’t run any faster!” With
a final burst of speed, Akito raced away and crossed
the finish line first.
After the race, all the boys except Jack came over
to talk to Akito. Jack had wandered off by himself,
looking very embarrassed.

title: Carnival Time

lines: The city of Mayberry has a carnival every year. It is
held in early spring when the weather is getting warm
again. The carnival is a very happy time. Most people
in the city like to take part in it.
The carnival always starts with a huge parade down
the main street of the city. An adult or child leads
the parade. This person is chosen because they have
done something special during the year. Everyone is
very proud of them.
There are many floats in the parade. They are
covered with flowers, balloons and flags. The floats
move slowly down the street. The people on the
floats dress in bright clothes. They wave and throw
flowers or streamers. The crowd claps and cheers as
the floats pass by.
Music and dancing are very important at carnival
time. Each school makes up songs and dances to
perform. There is a prize for the best school.
The parents help in many ways. They make
colourful costumes and masks, and teach the children
the new songs and dances. Everyone works hard
because they want their school to win.
In Mayberry Park, there are plenty of stalls where
people sell all kinds of things. Some people like the
food stalls best because they can buy fresh fruit,
sausages in bread, pink popcorn, delicious ice creams
and cold drinks.
People enjoy carnival time in Mayberry. Many say that
it is their favourite time of the year.

title: Saving Fresh Water
book_orientation: This text is an exposition. A girl gives reasons why it is important to save water.

lines: Did you know that the world could run out of fresh
water? It’s true. Already there are many countries
where people do not have enough fresh water to
drink.

We need to drink fresh water every day to survive. I
believe we all have to do something to save water.

waste in and around our homes. A lot of water is
wasted in the bathroom. Many people like to have
a bath instead of a shower. But it takes more water
to have a bath. Children often leave the tap running
when they are cleaning their teeth. If taps leak or are
not turned off properly, clean fresh water is lost. It
either runs down the pipes and out to the sea or it
soaks into the ground.
Second, we need to have a plan to save water.
When we are cleaning our teeth, we can wet the
brush and then turn the tap off while we are
brushing. We can have a shower instead of a bath.
Taps that are leaking need to be fixed as soon as
possible.
Finally, I think we should tell other people how we
are saving water. If people know that fresh water has
to be saved then I’m sure they will do something
about it, too.

wasn’t broken. After a few more tries I could control
it quite well. I even managed to make it turn and
dive without getting the lines tangled.
Tomorrow we are going back to the beach at low
tide to practise some more tricks.

title: How Seeds Spread
book_orientation: This text is an explanation about how seeds are spread.

lines: Seeds are spread in different ways. Some of them
travel long distances.
Wind can spread seeds. Many plants grow seed pods
that have hundreds of tiny seeds inside them. When
the pods are dry, they split open and tiny seeds fall
onto the ground. Many of them are blown away in
the wind. Some seeds float gently through the air for
great distances because they have small wings or little
fluffy parachutes.
Seeds are spread by birds and animals, too. Fruit and
vegetable seeds are spread when they pass through
the stomach of a bird or animal. This is often far
away from where the fruit or vegetables were eaten.
Sometimes seeds are spread when a bird or animal
walks on them. The seeds stick to their feet or
paws and fall off when the bird or animal moves to
another place. Some seeds have tiny hooks that cling
to the fur of many animals. These seeds drop off if
the animal rubs against something else, such as a tree
or a fence.
Some seeds are spread by water. When seeds fall into
water, they float along the surface until they are
washed up on a beach or a bank. Once the seeds
are in sand or soil, they begin to grow.
When seeds fall, they are often spread far away from
the shade of other plants. With plenty of sun and
water, these seeds grow into strong plants.

title: The Miller, His Son and Their Donkey
book_orientation: This text is a fable about a miller who was very foolish.

lines: A miller and his son were taking their donkey to
town to sell at a fair.
After a while, they passed some women. One of the
women said aloud, “Fancy walking, when you could
be riding your donkey!”
The miller told his son to ride the donkey. As they
continued along the road, they came upon two men,
deep in conversation. One of the men looked up
and spoke loudly to the other. “That lazy boy has no
respect for his father. The old man should be riding
the donkey.”
When the miller heard this, he made his son
dismount. Then he climbed onto the donkey instead.
They hadn’t gone far when they met another group
of people. “You selfish old man!” cried a woman,
pointing to the tired boy. At once, the miller pulled
his son up beside him.
The donkey trudged along with its heavy load. Soon
they met a traveller. “Your donkey is exhausted,” he
frowned. “You’ll have to carry it.”
The miller was so anxious to please the traveller that
he tied the donkey’s legs together. The miller and his
son carried it on a pole between them. As they
reached the edge of the town, people gathered
around, laughing loudly at this odd sight.
The donkey became very frightened by the noise. It
struggled wildly, until it broke the ropes and raced off
down the road.
“Oh, dear!” cried the miller. “I have been very foolish.
Why did I try to please everyone?”.

borrow.”

“I did it,” admitted the boy.
“I thought so,” said Kurt. “I’ll help you clean it
off when everyone has gone home, but you must
promise never to do it again.”

title: Sea Turtles
book_orientation: This text is an information report about sea turtles. Sea turtles are reptiles.

lines: Sea turtles belong to a group of animals called
reptiles. These turtles live all over the world, except
where the sea is very cold.
Sea turtles spend most of their lives underwater. They
can absorb oxygen from the water through their skin.
Sometimes they come up to the surface to breathe.
Although they often swim in shallow water where the
sea is warmed by the sun, they also swim across
huge oceans.
Sea turtles have thick scaly skin and a hard flat shell
which protects their bodies. They have large front
flippers that they use to push themselves through the
water.
Instead of having teeth, sea turtles have jaws that
are scissor-sharp. Many sea turtles feed on fish, crabs,
shellfish and jelly fish, while some eat only seaweeds
and sea grasses. A few eat poisonous sea sponges.
Scientists do not know how they can do this and
not die.
Most female turtles return to the beach where they
were born to lay their eggs. They dig shallow
nests above the high-tide mark. After laying their
eggs, they cover them with sand before returning to
the sea. Heat from the sun warms the sand where
the eggs lie buried. After hatching, the tiny turtles
wait only a few days before scuttling down the beach
towards the water’s edge. The waves carry those lucky
enough to reach the water out to sea.
Sea turtles have been on Earth for millions of years.
They are among the oldest animals in the world.

title: Why Brown Bears Hibernate
book_orientation: This text is an explanation about why brown bears hibernate.

lines: Brown bears are animals that hibernate. They
stay asleep for most of the winter because the
temperatures at this time of the year are extremely
cold.
Brown bears would die of hunger if they did not
hibernate. During the winter months, much of their
habitat is covered with ice and snow. Plants, berries
and fish are hard to find and it is difficult for the
bears to move around in the deep snow. So the
bears eat an enormous amount of food in autumn,
while there is plenty of it about. They grow quite fat
during this time.
Brown bears hibernate in a den that is warm and
dry. The den might be a cave or a hollow dug into
a steep bank. Sometimes the den is lined with sticks
and leaves.
When the bears hibernate, they are able to save
energy. They can survive in their dens all through the
winter months without needing to eat or drink. Their
heartbeat and breathing slow down because they do
not move around. The food they have eaten
in the autumn gives them enough energy to stay alive
through the whole winter season.
Brown bears hibernate for several months each year.
This is their way of adapting to the extremely cold
weather. After the winter, they emerge from their
dens, very hungry and ready to search for food again.

of smell!”

title: Preparation for a Hike
book_orientation: This text is a procedural recount. A boy recounts how he and his family prepared to go for a hike in the forest.

lines: Last summer, Dad took my sister and me hiking for
the day in the forest near his house. Before we left,
he explained that it was essential to be well prepared
for any emergency.
First, Dad made sure we were wearing the right
clothing. We wore long trousers and socks. This was
to protect our legs from insect bites and scratches
from the undergrowth. Dad told us to wear loose
shirts with long sleeves that we could roll up. Luckily,
all of us had comfortable walking boots. We wore
sunhats with brims, too. Just in case the weather
changed, we put waterproof jackets, warm sweaters
and woollen hats in our backpacks.
Then, we packed our lunch boxes with fruit, nuts
and sandwiches to eat during the day. We also put
in a few snacks, such as sweets and chocolate bars,
to give us energy. Our bottles were filled with fresh
water and placed in our packs where we could reach
them easily. We knew we had to drink water often to
prevent dehydration.
Next, Dad put his mobile phone and a small first-
aid kit in an outside pocket of his pack. I put the
sunscreen in mine.
Last of all, Dad checked the updated weather forecast
and he phoned a neighbour to let her know where
we were going and when we expected to return.
Because we had prepared well, we had an exciting
day exploring the forest. When we arrived back home,
Dad reminded us that we must never go hiking
alone.

I didn’t know if Mum would be able to see me but

armrests of her seat very tightly.

“Oh, thank you. That would be such a comfort,” she
said in a soft voice as she grasped my hand. “I’ve
flown before, but never in such a small plane. Once
we’re in the air, I’ll be all right.”

title: Sara’s Invitation
book_orientation: This text is a narrative. Chloe is delighted when she receives an invitation to Sara Forbes’ party.

lines: Flushed with excitement, Chloe raced into the kitchen
clutching a yellow envelope.
“I haven’t seen you so cheerful for days,” smiled her
mother, remembering how Chloe had moped about
the house for the past week.
“I’ve been invited to Sara Forbes’ party next Saturday,”
Chloe squealed excitedly, as she twirled around the
room, flapping the envelope. “I can’t believe Sara’s
actually picked me! She’s just chosen three of us.”
Chloe’s mother knew that every girl in Grade 5
desperately wanted to be Sara Forbes’ special friend.
“I’ll have to have a fabulous new dress for the party,”
declared Chloe.
“I’m sorry Chloe,” her mother said gently, “you know
we can’t possibly afford any additional expense at the
moment.”
“But Mum, I can’t wear my horrible old dress,”
Chloe said, her eyes welling with tears. “There’s never
enough money in this house to buy anything nice.”
“You know that’s not true, Chloe,” her mother replied,
giving her a hug.
Just at that moment, the phone rang and Mum went
into the next room to answer it. When she
returned she was smiling broadly.
“That was Sara’s mother,” she said. “She was just
phoning to say Sara really hopes you’ll come to her
party and to bring your swimming costume. She
forgot to tell you that you’re all going to the pool
before the barbecue party at the park.”
“Barbecue party!” exclaimed Chloe as she tore open
the yellow envelope. “So I won’t need that fabulous
new dress after all, will I?” she added with a
mischievous grin.

title: How Camels Survive in the Desert
book_orientation: This text is an explanation about how camels survive in the harsh conditions of a desert.

lines: The camel is a herbivore that inhabits desert regions
of the world. It has many special adaptations that
allow it to survive these harsh conditions.
Fat stored in the camel’s hump is used to provide
a source of energy. This means a camel is able to
last for long periods of time without food or water.
Because a camel can vary its body temperature, it
conserves water by not sweating.
To protect its eyes from the sand and wind, the
camel has two rows of long eyelashes. Special glands
secrete water to keep its eyes moist. The camel can
also close its nostrils to prevent sand blowing in.
The camel has thick, leathery skin on its knees to
protect them when it kneels on the sand. Its fur
is thick and woolly to provide warmth during the
cold desert nights, and insulation from high daytime
temperatures.
The camel’s long, thin legs help it to carry heavy
loads over incredibly long distances. They also keep
the camel’s body further from the hot sand.
The camel has broad, flat pads on its feet that
spread out when it walks. This prevents the camel
from sinking into the ground. The camel walks by
stepping with the two feet on the same side of its
body. This creates a rolling action, and has caused
camels to become known as “ships of the desert”.

title: Late Again!
book_orientation: This text is a narrative. A boy is late for an important baseball match.

lines: “Where’s Jared?” asked the captain, as the baseball
team boarded the bus.
“Oh, he’s late again,” protested Ben, “but let’s not wait
for him. A representative from the famous Allstars
team will be attending the match, and it’s not fair
to penalise all of us simply because one player can’t
organise himself properly. Besides, Jared’s always late
– late for school, late with homework and late for
training!”
The bus departed minus one team member, and as
it disappeared into the distance, Jared sprinted around
the corner.
“I can’t believe it!” he exclaimed. “I’m late again! I’ll
never get to the stadium in time, and I’ll definitely
have to think of an original excuse to tell everyone.”
As he contemplated his next move, a car pulled up
beside him. It was his coach! “Late again, I see!” he
teased. “Jump in, and we’ll give you a lift.”
It was then that Jared noticed an unfamiliar passenger.
Could it be…?
“Jared,” said the coach, “meet Tim Johnson, of the
Allstars.”
“Hi, Jared,” Tim said smoothly. He rummaged in
his bag and produced an autographed baseball cap.
“I decided I would present this souvenir to the
luckiest player today, and even before we get to the
game, you’ve taken the honours!” he grinned.
When the car came to a halt at the stadium, the
team swarmed around, anxious for an introduction.
Puzzled faces tinged with envy greeted Jared when he
stepped from the car wearing the signed cap.
“Please welcome Tim Johnson,” Jared beamed. “And, by
the way, my apologies for being late, but Tim’s plane
was delayed!”

title: The Haircut
book_orientation: This text is a narrative. A girl’s parents react to her new hairstyle.

lines: Tentatively, I opened the front door and walked
inside, expecting a fairly explosive reaction to my new
hairstyle. I sauntered into the lounge room, where
Dad was reclining with the daily newspaper. He leapt
from his seat when he saw me.
“What’s this?” he demanded. He circled me like a
lion stalking its prey, totally stunned at the modern
combination of streaks and spikes I had chosen. “You
should be ashamed of yourself! What on earth would
make you do something like that?” he continued, his
voice mixed with astonishment and dread.
Mum came in from the kitchen to see what all the
fuss was about. Her jaw dropped and she stared at
me disbelievingly. “But… but I thought… oh, Eliza!”
she said, her voice barely a whisper. “Why?”
“Don’t worry, Mum,” I said, hoping she would see
this situation from my perspective. “A hairstyle isn’t
permanent, you know.”
“This is just ridiculous,” Dad raved on, “I thought you
had more common sense!”
His outburst lasted for several more minutes, until
Mum was more concerned with calming him than
worrying about my fashion sense.
When Dad finally returned to his favourite chair, and
the mood had become a little more subdued, I knew
the time was right. I put my hand to my hair and in
one swift movement, lifted off the wig and shook my
head, allowing the silky, auburn curls to softly frame
my face.
“Do you like my haircut?” I enquired enthusiastically.
“I do, but I thought the wig was more appropriate
for the school disco tonight!”

title: Vehicle Pollution
book_orientation: This text is a discussion. It gives reasons for and against different ways to reduce vehicle pollution.

lines: Every day, exhaust fumes from fuel-driven vehicles
pollute the air. Many people believe pollution can
only be reduced by having fewer vehicles on our
roads. Others disagree. They say this would be very
difficult for people who require vehicles for work and
other essential transport. They believe that, instead,
drivers must make an effort to use less fuel.
Those people who argue for fewer vehicles on our
roads say one way to achieve this is to improve
public transport. Bus lanes that bypass heavy traffic
could be built and extra trains could operate at peak
times. These improvements will encourage people who
work in the city to leave their cars at home. As well,
they think more people should attempt to carpool,
use bicycles or walk. Older vehicles should be tested
and if their pollution levels are too high, they should
not be allowed on the road at all.
Other people argue that by using less fuel we would
create less vehicle pollution. Smaller cars, new cars and
older vehicles that are regularly serviced use less fuel.
Drivers save fuel by switching off engines when
they stop for any length of time. Furthermore, they
save fuel by having wheel pressures checked, car boots
emptied and roof racks removed when they are not
in use.
I agree with those people who support having fewer
vehicles on our roads. But I also believe drivers must
be encouraged to use less fuel if vehicle pollution
from exhaust fumes is to be reduced.

title: Plastic in Our World
book_orientation: This is a non-fiction text. It is an exposition of the writer’s opinion of why we should use less plastic.

lines: Good morning class.
My talk is about plastic. There are many things made
from plastic that we use every day. But people all
over the world are careless. They leave plastic things
they no longer want on the land and in the water.
Plastic doesn’t rot in soil or water. This means that
plastic rubbish could stay around for hundreds of
years. Sometimes, birds and small animals get caught
in pieces of plastic and they die.
Fish and other sea animals are often trapped in
plastic that is thrown from boats. They cannot get
free and they starve or drown.
Many plastic toys crack or break after children have
played with them for a short time. My favourite toys
are wooden ones that my grandad makes for me. He
says they will last much longer than plastic ones.
Shop owners like people to use cloth or strong paper
bags to carry fruit, meat and other goods.
I agree with them! These bags can be used over and
over again.
My mum used to line our rubbish bin with a plastic
bag. But now she uses newspaper instead. It is much
better than plastic.
I believe we can all help to look after the land and
the sea if we try to think of other ways to use less
plastic.

title: Bushfires
book_orientation: This is a non-fiction text. It is an information report about bushfires.

lines: A fire that starts in a bush or forest is a bushfire. A
bushfire usually begins when dry leaves or small twigs
are set alight by a spark from a match or from
lightning.
In places where the land is very hot and dry,
bushfires spread quickly. Dry undergrowth on the
forest floor catches fire first. Then the fire spreads up
tree trunks to the large branches. Strong winds blow
sparks from one tree to the next. Before long, a
large part of the bush can burst into flames.
People who put out bushfires are called fire fighters.
They travel from the nearest fire station to the
bushfire in a truck. The truck is fitted with long
hoses. Water from a tank on the truck is pumped
onto the fire until it stops burning. Helicopters
with large fire buckets are used to control some
huge fires.
Bushfires can be fierce. Sometimes people have to
move out of their homes if a fire comes too
close. Wildlife can get caught in bushfires and
die. When trees are burnt, birds and small animals
have to find somewhere else to live.
Some plants need heat and smoke from a fire
for their seeds to grow. So, after a bushfire, new
green shoots can often be seen sprouting from the
blackened ground.

lines: Friday, 17 October
Before I left for school yesterday, Mum warned me
that there would be heavy rain all day. She was
right. During the morning, the gutters outside our
classroom overflowed, and soon the school field
looked like an enormous lake.
By late afternoon, we were told that the river had
burst its banks. It had flooded across the valley road.
That meant the school bus wouldn’t be able to get
through. No one could go home. We were trapped
here for the night.
At first, everyone thought that it was exciting,
but then we realised we had nothing left to eat.
We huddled together in a classroom, feeling a bit
miserable, and watched a DVD.
At five o’clock, we heard a truck pull up outside
the school. Mr Hill, who owns the farm next to
the school, had brought food and hot drinks for us.
Everybody felt much better after that.
Then, about an hour later, we couldn’t believe our
eyes when a helicopter landed in the playground. The
pilot had blankets, sleeping bags and lots
more food for us. Two parents came as well.
They remained with us to help the teachers.
When we woke up this morning, the water had gone
down far enough for the school bus to take us home
safely. The flood in the valley was the best adventure
I’ve ever had.

on, Steve said, “I thought she’d find snowboarding
easy. She’s a natural.”

laughed Zoe.

title: Why a River Floods
book_orientation: This is a non-fiction text. It is an explanation of why a river floods.

lines: A river is a long stream of flowing water. It has
banks on either side. A river floods when there is
more water flowing in it than it can hold. The
extra water spills over the banks and spreads across
the land.
Water that causes a flood can come from rainfall.
When there is a small amount of rain, land near a
river can soak up some of the water.
But if there is more rain than usual, the soil, trees
and grass nearby cannot soak it all up. The water
that is not soaked up runs into the river.
Floods can also be caused by melted snow or by
water from a dam that has a break in the wall.
If the land beside the flooded river is flat, the extra
water can spread quickly. It will cover a large area in
a short time.
Floods can damage buildings or ruin crops.
Then people may have nowhere to live and no food
to eat. Sometimes people drown in floods. The water
level often rises very quickly. There is not always
enough time to warn people to move to higher land.
However, not all floods cause problems. Sometimes
a flood leaves a layer of fine soil on the surface of
the land. This soil is very good for growing the next
season’s crops.

embarrassing for the dog owner, as well.
I believe that owners should keep their dogs on leads
in public places. People would feel safer, there would
be fewer traffic accidents and neighbours would be
happier.

the tree outside Lucy’s window scraped against the
pane. Suddenly, the dark sky was split in two by a

She shivered and hid her head under the bed covers.
She was afraid – in fact, very frightened now. Storms

Lucy wondered if she should go down to the stable
and check on Star, her new pony. He would be very
nervous. She imagined him pacing around in his box;

coming from the stable, the sky lit up bright yellow,

downstairs. She was just opening the back door when
she saw the shadow of something moving by the
corner of the house. It couldn’t be Rusty the
dog, because Dad had made sure he was securely
tied up in the shed.
Next thing, a dark figure, bent over against the
strong wind, came towards her. Lucy stiffened, then,
with a sense of relief, she realised it was her father.
He had been worried about Star, too.

title: Charlie
book_orientation: This is a fiction text. It is a narrative about a brother and sister who hear the sound of a dog barking as they walk home from school.

lines: Yesterday, when Brent and Angie were walking home
from school, they heard the sound of a ferocious dog
barking. An elderly man had moved into the vacant
house a few doors away from where they lived, so
they presumed the dog belonged to him.
“I’m scared, Brent,” Angie admitted. “I hope that dog
doesn’t run out and attack us!”
“It’s okay, Angie,” Brent said reassuringly. “Let’s walk
quickly and we’ll soon be home.”
The next afternoon, when they neared the house
again, they heard a savage growl, “Grrr… grrr… grrr!”
Angie was really frightened. She clung to her brother’s
arm and hid behind him, shaking with fear.
“Come on, let’s hurry,” Brent suggested. Neither of
them wanted to come face-to-face with a creature
that could make a terrifying noise like that!
Just as they quickened their pace and were about to
make a hasty detour across the road, the front door
of the house was flung open.
“Run!” Brent shouted. He pictured an enormous dog,
with razor sharp teeth, charging out of the house,
clearing the fence and attacking them. But instead of
a ferocious dog, the owner emerged with a cockatoo
perched on his shoulder.
“Hello!” the cockatoo squawked. “Grrr… woof… woof…
woof!” it barked.
“Oh, it’s only a bird!” Angie laughed. “I thought you
had a savage dog,” she said to the man.
“No! This is Charlie,” the man smiled, as he scratched
the yellow comb on top of the cockatoo’s head.

title: How a Parachute Works
book_orientation: This is a non-fiction text. It is an explanation of how a parachute helps a parachutist fall safely to the ground after jumping from an aircraft.

lines: A parachute is a light-weight device that is designed
to slow the fall of a person during a descent to
Earth. Parachutes act like air brakes.
Before entering the aircraft, the parachutist checks his
main parachute to make sure it will open properly
when he needs it. He also checks the reserve
parachute. This is packed underneath the main
chute for use in case of an emergency. These two
parachutes are in a special type of backpack which
the parachutist wears when he jumps.
Once the aircraft is high enough in the air, the
parachutist prepares for his jump. When the pilot
gives the signal, the parachutist knows he can jump
out safely.
At the right time during the descent, the parachutist
pulls a rip-cord on his backpack. This releases the
canopy of the main parachute. The canopy inflates
with air and the parachute glides forward and down.
The parachutist steers the parachute by pulling on
handles on either side of the chute. As he
nears the ground, the parachutist turns the parachute
into the wind. This helps him land slowly.
A parachute is very light and has a large surface area
like the wings on a bird. The canopy fills with air
and resists the force of gravity, allowing the parachute
to fall slowly and safely to the ground.

title: The Wallet
book_orientation: This is a narrative about two boys and an important decision they have to make.

lines: “I’ll meet you at the sports shop in about fifteen
minutes,” Connor’s mother called to the boys
cheerfully, as they entered the shopping complex. “I’m
going into the clothing shop next door.”
Connor and James darted off to look at the new
season’s footy boots.
“I really need a new pair, but I don’t have enough
pocket money,” James said dejectedly.

the floor. James stooped to pick it up and tentatively
peered inside. He glanced at Connor in disbelief as he
flicked through the wad of notes.

to buy new footy boots,” James calculated. “Nobody
can see us here because we’re hidden by that rack of
clothes!” he reasoned. “What do you think we should
do, Connor?” he asked, looking at Connor uneasily.
Connor briefly considered their options, then said
firmly, “We both know what we should do.”
James nodded in agreement.

manager appeared before them. “We found this wallet
on the floor,” James said defensively.
“Yes, I know; I was observing you from my office on
the in-store security camera,” the manager explained.
At that moment, Connor’s mum came into the shop.
She saw the manager holding the wallet.
“These boys have been very honest,” the manager
reassured her, “and I’m rewarding them with a
voucher to spend in my shop!”

title: Wind Power
book_orientation: This is a non-fiction text. It is a discussion about reasons for and against building more wind farms.

lines: I think wind power will one day replace coal and
oil as an important producer of electricity. My father
doesn’t agree. He accepts that supplies of coal and
oil throughout the world will run out, but he doesn’t
think wind power is the answer to the problem.
I believe we should be building more wind farms
because wind will continue to blow as long as the
sun warms Earth. Once they are built, wind farms
need only steady winds to spin the huge blades that
make electricity.
Wind power is safe, too. It does not add poisonous
gases to the air. I don’t think people in cities will be
concerned when large wind farms are built nearby.
My father says wind farms would not produce enough
electricity for daily use in large cities. Factories need a
lot of electricity. He also thinks that the noise of the
wind farms would upset most people.
He believes wind farms would have to be built where
the wind is strongest if they are to produce sufficient
electricity. This is likely to be on land required
for farming and he says land for agriculture is too
valuable for use as wind farms.
Although my father doesn’t think wind power will
ever be an important producer of electricity, I think
it will. In the years to come, I believe more and
more wind farms will have to be built to supply
our needs.

side door, and from this angle immediately noticed
the ignition wire was unplugged. In no time he’d
connected it, and on the next attempt the engine
roared to life.

complimented him. “From now on, I’ll have to call
you Dr Max!”

title: Tracking Giant Petrels
book_orientation: This is a non-fiction text. It is a recount in the form of a journal entry outlining the procedure that an Antarctic scientist would use to attach transmitters to giant petrels.

lines: 22 January
Although there was a blustery wind on Humble Island
today, the weather was generally fine. My job was to
attach tiny satellite-tracking transmitters to adult giant
petrels. I’d been unable to do this yesterday because
the tape wouldn’t stick to the birds’ damp feathers.
I had to claw my way over jagged rocks on the
south side of the island to reach one of the nests I
was looking for. A male giant petrel was still sitting
on it. His female mate had not yet returned from a
foraging trip.
At first, I spent some time speaking soothingly to the
bird. This helped to keep him calm. Then I gently
removed the fragile egg he was sitting on and quickly
replaced it with a white wooden egg.
I waited a moment to see if he would react, but
he remained quiet. So I carefully lifted some of the
feathers on his back and pressed a small plastic
transmitter to them. Next, I wrapped sticky
tape tightly around the bundle and added two
nylon cable ties. This made everything secure. Then
I adjusted the short aerial on the transmitter before
finally replacing the real egg.
The transmitter will send data on this bird’s precise
location for up to 115 days. This data will be used
to help track where these enormous birds forage
when outside the nesting area.
